    Danger zone

    Privacy & legal

    What this game stores

    Kaido Drift sets no cookies. It keeps one entry in your browser's local storage on this device: a random player ID, your driver name, credits, owned cars, paint choices and settings. That entry is strictly necessary for the game to remember your progress and never leaves your device. There are no ads, no analytics and no third-party trackers.

    The only network requests are for the game's code library (three.js from the jsDelivr CDN) and its fonts (Google Fonts). Those providers can see your IP address as part of any normal web request.

    You can erase everything at any time under Settings → Erase progress, or by clearing this site's data in your browser.

    AI drivers

    The other drivers and every chat message they send are computer-controlled and marked AI. Nothing you type in chat is sent anywhere; it stays on your device.

    Trademarks

    Kaido Drift is an independent fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Nissan, Toyota, Mazda or any other manufacturer. Every car, maker name and logo in the game is an original, fictional design. Chassis-style codes are used only as era references.

    Licence

    Game code and art are original and generated procedurally in your browser. three.js is used under the MIT licence. Fonts (Dela Gothic One, Chakra Petch) are used under the SIL Open Font Licence.

    Map data

    Terrain is real elevation data for Hakone and Mt. Fuji at 1:1 scale from Terrain Tiles on AWS (Mapzen / Linux Foundation), derived from NASA SRTM, USGS GMTED2010 and NOAA ETOPO1. The road layout, buildings and trees are the game's own design placed on that terrain; they are not a survey of real roads.

    Onlineオンライン

    Drive with real people on a Kaido Drift server and chat with them. Other players' cars are ghosts: you can drift together, but you can't crash into each other.

    Be kind in chat. Messages are shared with everyone on the server. Type /mute name to hide a player's messages, or /unmute name to show them again.
